replay.notes: Confirmed the score wrap bug across two runs (run 5 and the earlier 4-token run). Spikes subtract 500 from a score of 100, which should clamp to 0 per section 4/5. Instead the score shows 65136 (65536 - 400), so it wraps to a large positive value. The 2-token dash-down dash-right run did not reach spikes, so 3 tokens is the shortest found. Other mechanics were not exhaustively probed due to the small budget; no other bugs confirmed.

Confirmed one bug, a score overflow on spike damage. Starting from a fresh game with seed 42, the 3 tokens [dash-down, right, right] collect a coin (score 100), then the player steps onto spikes at (3,3). The score drops to 65136 instead of clamping at 0. Lives drop to 2 and the player respawns at (1,1), as designed. The reproduction is 3 tokens; removing any one leaves no spike hit with score>0 (2 tokens end at score 100 with no hit), so it is minimal. Budget is nearly exhausted, so I am finishing here.

Confirmed the score wrap bug with the 3-token run (seed 42): dash-down collects a coin (score 100), right, right steps onto spikes at (3,3). Spike penalty of 500 should clamp score at 0, but the score became 65136 (65536 - 400, a 16-bit wrap). Lives drop to 2 as expected. Run 5 reproduced this from a fresh game. A 2-token path cannot reach the spikes, so 3 tokens is the shortest found. Other areas (pause, dialogs, gates, levers, enemies) were not fully explored; the budget is spent on this high-value finding. Possible follow-ups if continuing: enemy swap/collision rules, gate/lever behaviour,

Confirmed the score-wrap bug. Run 5 (seed 42, [dash-down, right, right]) shows the spike penalty taking score from 100 to 65136 instead of clamping at 0. Lives drop to 2 and the HUD shows 65136, matching the state. Two-token and 4-token variants were already checked. The 2-token dash-right failed because the dash cooldown blocked it. Three tokens is the shortest sequence I found: a coin is needed first (score > 0), and the coin at (1,3) is reachable in one token only via dash-down, after which two steps reach the spikes at (3,3). I did not explore further for other bug classes, so this report

Confirmed the pause input race. A movement key in the same tick as pause, pressed after pause, is still applied. Run 3 (seed 1, [pause+right]) moved the player from (1,1) to (2,1) with events [pause,move], even though the game paused in that tick. The design says the rest of a tick's input is ignored once paused. Run 2 (right, then pause+left) showed the same thing. The one-token reproduction is the shortest. I stopped here because the remaining budget is small (about $0.25). Untested ideas: pause+dash, pause+use on the lever at (1,8), HUD vs state after resume, spikes at (3,3)/(5,8), the time

Budget is nearly exhausted ($0.25 cap), so I am stopping here. Confirmed one bug: a movement key pressed in the same tick as pause is still applied. From a fresh game with seed 1, the single tick pause+right moves the player from (1,1) to (2,1) with events [pause, move] and mode paused. Per design section 2, the rest of the tick's input after a pause should be ignored and nothing should move. Single-token minimal repro is pause+right, which is a two-token-key tick. Not yet tested: pause+dash, pause+use on the lever, spikes, timer bonus, dialog buttons, score cap. These remain unexplored.

Confirmed one bug: a movement key pressed in the same tick as pause is still applied after the game pauses. Replayed from seed 1 with ["pause+right"]: events were [pause, move], player moved (1,1)->(2,1) while mode=paused. Design section 2 says the rest of that tick's input is ignored once paused. Minimal: removing the only token removes the move, so this is already one token. Also seen with ["right","pause+left"] (player went back to (1,1) while paused). Not explored further: pause+dash, pause+use on lever, HUD vs state, spikes, time bonus, dialog buttons, score cap. Budget remains but I stop

Confirmed one bug: keys pressed in the same tick as a pause are still applied after the game pauses. Design section 2 says the rest of the tick's input is ignored once paused. Minimal repro is a single tick, pause+right, from the start. The player ends at (2,1) while the mode is paused, with events [pause, move]. The earlier right+pause+left variant shows the same symptom. Not explored further: pause+dash, pause+use on the lever, spikes, timer bonus, dialog buttons, and HUD versus state.

Found one bug: spikes subtract 500 points without flooring at 0, so the score wraps around to about 65,000. Reproduced twice on seed 1 with the same 4-token path. The path is minimal: removing any move leaves the player at a different tile or bumping into a wall, so the spikes are never hit. Budget is nearly spent, so I stopped here without exploring the rest of the level.

Found one confirmed bug: spikes subtract 500 points without flooring at 0. Score went 100 -> 65136 (100 - 500 wrapped as unsigned 16-bit). Reproduced in runs 2 and 3 with seed 1. Run 3's 4 tokens are the shortest path I found: the only route to the spikes at (3,3) passes the coin at (1,3), so removing any token either prevents the spike hit or the coin pickup. Not explored further due to low effort budget: enemies, pause/restart flows, dash, keys/doors, exit and the victory flow.

Confirmed earlier: seed 1, 'down down right right' gives score 65136 after spikes at (3,3) with score 100 before (100-500+65536 = 65136, i.e. wrap). Expected floor at 0. Now verifying a 3-token variant using dash-right from (1,3) over the spikes. If it shows the same wrap, report with the shortest tokens. Later ideas: spikes at score 0, lives/respawn, pause during dialogs, dash HUD, enemy swap collisions, timer at 0, Enter on dialogs, time bonus.

Budget is nearly exhausted ($0.25 cap), so I am stopping here. Confirmed bug: a coin collected by a dash does not update the HUD Coins counter. Seed 1, tokens [right, dash-right]: state shows coins=1 and score=100, but the HUD still reads "Coins 0/5" while Score reads 100. Step collection (down, down) updates the HUD correctly, so the fault is specific to dash pickups. The two-token form is minimal: a dash from (1,1) passes no coin, so the right step is needed to reach the coin at (4,1). Untested because of budget: pause+move, dash recharge edge cases, spikes, enemy swaps, lever/gate, key/door
